selections.title: NTP over IPv6 - Operating as an NTP server.
selections.justification:
Step: Ensure DUT clock synronized via NTP
Expected: NTP Status is synconised

Step: Start NTP client devices.
Note their NTP association and status
Expected: NTP Clients show a valid and association with the DUT as master.

selections.title: NTP over IPv6 - Operating as an NTP server.
selections.justification:
Objective: NTP will respond to any NTP packets (unless the ingress packets are blocked by other processes - i.e. clasifiers)
NTP will respond appropriatly regardless what transport protocol the packets arrive on.

Precondition: DUT configured with several IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces.
Oher devices configured to use the DUT as an NTP server via IPv6 and/or IPv4.
DUT configured to us 1 or more external NTP servers via IPv6.

Status: Approved | Has objective: True | Num steps: 3 | Labels: Operational

Steps:
1. Ensure DUT clock synronized via NTP
2. Start NTP client devices.
Note their NTP association and status
3. check show command

selections.title: NTP on VRF - Check that NTP client/server associations work when configured over a VRF
selections.justification:
Objective: client server - both ends configured with NTP over a VRF vlan

Precondition: Wire as follows: [Client]----[DUT]----[NTP server] Configure appropriate IP addressing and routing on each of the devices above Ensure that the L3 interfaces on DUT are in a named VRF Configure NTP server as a server by using the "ntp master" command. Use the "ntp server [IP address of DUT]" command on "Client"

Status: Approved | Has objective: True | Num steps: 1

Steps:
1. use the command "ntp server vrf [VRF name] [IP address of NTP server]" on the DUT

step4.objective:
• Device configured with an IPv6 address on the NTP server interface, with NTP enabled and operating in server mode over IPv6
  • NTP server responds to NTPv4 client requests received over IPv6 transport
  • Server advertises correct stratum, reference ID, and reference timestamp in NTP response packets sent over IPv6
  • Time synchronisation information provided by the IPv6 NTP server is accurate and consistent with the server's system clock
  • NTP server continues to operate correctly over IPv4 simultaneously when dual-stack is configured
  • NTP server does not respond to malformed or unsupported NTP packet types received over IPv6
  • NTP server rejects or ignores requests from IPv6 clients not permitted by configured access restrictions
  • NTP associations and statistics for IPv6 clients are correctly displayed in show/status commands
  • NTP server operation over IPv6 persists correctly across a device reboot or NTP service restart
  • Relevant log entries or system messages are generated reflecting NTP server state changes and IPv6 client associations

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
From an IPv6-connected NTPv4 client, send time synchronisation requests to the DUT's NTP service. Confirm the server processes the requests and returns responses over the IPv6 transport.
Capture or inspect the NTP response packets returned to the IPv6 client and examine the stratum, reference identifier, and reference timestamp fields carried in those responses.

Compare the time value and reference timestamp conveyed to the IPv6 client against the DUT's own system clock at the time of the exchange, repeating the comparison after some elapsed interval to confirm ongoing consistency.
With the NTP server interface configured as dual-stack, have an IPv4 client and an IPv6 client query the server concurrently. Confirm both address families are served without one affecting the other.

From an IPv6 client, send malformed NTP packets and packets of unsupported or unexpected NTP message types to the server. Confirm the server's handling of these inputs, including whether any response is produced.

Configure an access restriction on the DUT that excludes a specific IPv6 client or address range from NTP service, then have that client attempt to query the server while a permitted IPv6 client queries it as well.
With one or more IPv6 clients actively associated with the server, inspect the DUT's NTP association and statistics information to confirm the IPv6 client entries are represented.

With an active IPv6 NTP server configuration and at least one IPv6 client association established, restart the NTP service (or reboot the device) and confirm the server resumes serving IPv6 clients and associations are re-established afterwards.

Trigger NTP server state changes over IPv6, such as enabling/disabling the service, applying or removing an access restriction, and establishing a new client association, then inspect the DUT's logs or system messages for entries corresponding to each change.

gaps: No ATPyLib (ART) automated tests have been identified as covering this case, leaving the NTP-over-IPv6 server role entirely without automation coverage. The manual intent captured in AWPTCM-T44298 and its related artefacts (AWPTCM-T10517, AWPTCM-T33633) spans DUT clock synchronisation status verification, multi-client NTP association behaviour, and NTP operation over a VRF context, none of which are exercised by automation at present. Key gaps include observability of NTP synchronisation state transitions, correctness of client association reporting across multiple simultaneous clients, and the interaction between IPv6 NTP server behaviour and VRF-scoped configurations. Given the medium weighting of this decision, this represents a moderate but unaddressed risk area requiring either new automated test development or continued reliance on manual execution.
